It feels almost automatic in the moment, and then afterward I’m disgusted with myself and really guilty.

To “fix” it, I’ve been taking laxative pills more than I’m supposed to. I tell myself it’s just to not feel so bloated, but I know I’m mainly doing it because I’m scared of gaining weight. Lately I’ve also been more down, tired, and just not really enjoying things the way I used to, but I’m not sure if that’s just stress or something else.

When I come back to myself, there’s wrappers everywhere and I feel stupid and a bit ashamed.

Then I worry I’m going to get bigger and slower. In the mirror I see this thick, heavy man, like my belly is sticking out far more than it probably does. My daughter says I’m “fine for my age,” but I don’t see that. I keep thinking, “You’re getting huge.”

So I’ve been taking those over‑the‑counter tablets to, you know, keep things moving. More than the box says, especially after those nights. I know I probably shouldn’t, but it makes me feel like I’m undoing some of the damage.

Most days I just feel flat, tired, not much interest in anything, and I’m alone with these habits I don’t really understand.

My mood hasn’t been great either. I’m more withdrawn, not really interested in meeting friends or dating. A lot of how I see myself as a person seems tied up in whether I feel “in control” of my body and how I look, and lately I mostly just feel like I’m failing at that.

I’ve been struggling for maybe… the last couple of months? It’s hard to pin down exactly. I’m still functioning at work — I’m the head nurse on nights — but it feels like I’m on autopilot most of the time. When I get home after a shift, that’s when things really get away from me.
